statement: For every complete finite simple SRG(99,14,1,2), the number R of distinct induced nine-vertex subsets isomorphic to the3-by-3 rook graph satisfies0<=R<=231 and R!=230. For each actual triangle T, its rook multiplicity r_T yields d_T=6-r_T; at every v in T the simple graph on the seven triangles through v, joining pairs not together contained in an induced rook-nine, has degree d_T at T. These nonnegative deficiencies sum to6*(231-R), and their odd support has even incidence at every point. The count231 and hypothetical target existence are not excluded.

scope.description: Universal necessary induced-rook/actual-triangle incidence identities for complete simple SRG(99,14,1,2) graphs, with the specific deficiency-six packing gap. Count actual nine-subsets, not embeddings, automorphisms or disjoint copies. No fixed-profile restriction or target realization/exclusion.

assumptions: The graph is complete finite simple SRG(99,14,1,2), with all actual triangles used once.
R counts distinct induced nine-vertex rook subsets. r_T counts all such subsets containing actual triangle T.
A defect edge means no such rook contains both incident triangles; absence of a defect edge requires actual rook existence, not merely a proposed completion.
The theorem does not assume an automorphism, a uniform external profile, a triangle factor or an N3-free target.
dependency_reason: The paper derives triangle incidence, unique-pair and C4 reconstruction,6R/9R counts, defect degrees and even-six classification directly from the stated graph hypotheses. The historical rook and binary-image proofs are overlap/provenance comparisons, not inherited approval for this statement.
identities: sum_(T containing v) d_T is even
sum_T d_T>=4*d_U for every positive-deficiency triangle U
boundaries: Rook9 itself has an even six-triangle dependency and zero analogous local defect degrees; even-six dependencies are not generally forbidden.
AtR231 all d_T are zero; this proof has no contradiction and does not supplyR<=229.
A fourfold point among six selected triangles needs eight outer incidences from only six available remaining incidences.
A dual cubic triangle-free six-node graph is K3,3; any extra point-graph edge violateslambda1 because it already has two rook common neighbors.
Two intersecting actual triangles determine at most one rook via the uniquely fixed second common neighbors of their four cross pairs. Existence is not claimed.
Overlapping rook subsets are counted exactly by incidence double counting; disjointness is not assumed.
An uncovered C4 is not asserted to force N3 or a universal grid cover.
